title: S1 V3.9 / S2 V3.2 — prior one/two completed daily bars
question: Do the directions of the prior one and two fully completed XAUUSD daily bars affect the original outcomes of current S1 V3.9 and S2 V3.2 trades, alone or alongside post-signal confirmation?
hypothesis: Because both strategies are long-only, recent daily direction may change setup quality, but any interaction must use completed bars and must be validated separately rather than multiplying probabilities.

findings.title: A prior down day is associated with better long-strategy outcomes
findings.detail: S1 D-1 DOWN was 59.52% WR (n=210) versus 53.33% after UP (n=240); S2 was 50.57% (n=87) versus 42.86% (n=70). This may reflect pullback/reversal opportunity, not causal trend continuation.

findings.title: The D-1 direction remained aligned in the latest 30%
findings.detail: Held-out S1 was 60.87% after DOWN versus 46.97% after UP (69/66 trades); held-out S2 was 41.67% versus 25.0% (24/24 trades). S2's overall recent regime was weak, so the context does not rescue the strategy by itself.

findings.title: S1's UP→DOWN two-day sequence is the most stable sequence
findings.detail: S1 UP→DOWN was 63.64% WR across 132 trades and stayed nearly identical in the early 70% (63.83%) and recent 30% (63.16%). S2 did not show the same stable two-day ranking.

findings.title: Combined daily × intraday cells become too small for hard rules
findings.detail: Many S2 interaction cells are below n=20. Daily direction is best treated as context for a later replay, not multiplied with the 30-minute percentage and not used as a binary gate.
